newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican lower house approves petrochemical plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexican lower house approves petrochemical plan.

text.p: Mexico's Chamber of Deputies voted 277 to 144 on Wednesday to approve the government's revised scheme for the sale of state-owned petrochemical plants, a spokesman from the lower legislative house said.
The legislation to approve the petrochemical industry's partial privatisation now passes to the Senate before receiving the signature of President Ernesto Zedillo.
The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party controls both legislative chambers.
Earlier this month the government decided to offer private and foreign investors a 49 percent stake in Mexico's 61 petrochemical plants, rather than 100 percent as originally planned.
The switch followed highly charged public debate over the fate of the plants, currently owned by state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos.
